um: Expression of hesitation, uncertainty or space filler in conversation.
umangite: A selenide mineral, with chemical formula Cu₃Se₂, blue to red in color.
umbel: A flat-topped or rounded flower-cluster (= inflorescence) in which the individual flower stalks arise from the same point, the youngest flowers being at the centre.
umbellar: Of, pertaining to, bearing or having the form of an umbel.
umbellet: A secondary umbel in a compound umbel such as the carrot; an umbellule.
umbellifer: Any plant of the family Apiaceae, also called Umbelliferae, whose inflorescence is an umbel, such as a carrot or celery.
umber: A brown clay, somewhat darker than ochre, which contains iron and manganese oxides.
umbered: simple past and past participle of umber
umbering: present participle and gerund of umber
umbilical: Of, or relating to, the navel (umbilicus) or the umbilical cord.
umbilication: A small, navel-shaped depression, or dimple, at the centre of a rounded body.
umbles: Animal entrails, especially of a deer.
umbo: The boss of a shield, at or near the middle and usually projecting, sometimes in a sharp spike.
umbra: The fully shaded inner region of a shadow cast by an opaque object.
umbrage: A feeling of anger or annoyance caused by something offensive.
umbral: Of or relating to an umbra.
umbrella: A cloth-covered frame used for protection against rain or sun.
umbrellaed: Covered by or carrying an umbrella.
umbrellaing: present participle and gerund of umbrella
umbrette: Synonym of hammerkop (Scopus umbretta, a bird)
umiak: A large, open boat made of skins stretched over a wooden frame that is propelled by paddles; used by the Eskimos for transportation.
umlaut: An assimilatory process whereby a vowel is pronounced more like a following vocoid that is separated by one or more consonants.
umlauted: simple past and past participle of umlaut
umlauting: present participle and gerund of umlaut
umped: simple past and past participle of ump
umping: present participle and gerund of ump
umpirage: The office (or term of office) of an umpire
umpire: An official who presides over a sports match.
umpired: simple past and past participle of umpire
umpiring: present participle and gerund of umpire
umpteen: Relatively large but unspecified in number.
umpteenth: Occurring in a relatively large but unspecified position in a sequence.
